### problem_chain

**Root.** The customer raises one thing: he wants to keep the skis until 2027-02-23 rather than bringing them back on the 18th. That is `rentals_ext_extension_charge` (`trigger: on_request`, `computes: extension_charge_usd`, `subject: [rentals_extend, rentals_fee_charge]`, target `confirm_rental_extension_b56bb368`, `owner="user"`). Base `rentals_swap_and_extension` admits it: the Basic package carries `extension_allowed: true` and `extension_max_days: 7`, the kit is still out, and *"An extension is recorded before the kit falls due"* — `due_date 2027-02-18` has not passed at `NOW 2027-02-17`.

**Hop 1.** The root's rule carries: *"The charge for the extra days is fixed only after the hire rate for the days the agreement was written for stands on its rental account."* Does that state hold? `rentals_ledger` carries exactly one `rentals_rate_charge` row, `1870efd2…`, and its `charge_category` is `helmet_addon`, not the hire rate; `rentals_holdings.rental_balance_usd = 60.00` equals that helmet add-on alone, confirming no hire rate has been raised. **Unmet.** The only rule in the charter that says how the hire rate for an agreement is arrived at is `rentals_ext_party_rate_charge`; its write is `raise_rental_rate_charge_fcd244c0`. Edge kind `value_input` — it decides `rate_charged`, which selects which basis the extra-day figure is taken on.

**Hop 2.** The root's rule also carries: *"The charge for the extra days is fixed only after every change of model recorded on the agreement carries the shop's fee owed for it."* `rentals_holdings.swap_count = 1` and `rentals_requests.499652cb…` (`request_type: size_change`, `outcome: confirmed`, created 2027-02-15) record one change of model; `rentals_ledger` carries **no** `rentals_fee_charge` row at all, so no change carries a fee. **Unmet.** Resolved by `rentals_ext_model_change_fee` → `raise_model_change_fee_b751c3b4`. Edge kind `value_input` — it decides `change_fee_entries`, which decides `extension_fee_due`.

Neither `party_rate_charge` nor `model_change_fee` carries a prerequisite sentence of its own; the walk terminates.

**Tree derived from the policy and the world alone:**

```
rentals_ext_extension_charge                (root, USER write)
  ├── rentals_ext_party_rate_charge         value_input, agent write
  └── rentals_ext_model_change_fee          value_input, agent write
```

n = 2 prerequisite problems; floor is max(2−1,1) = 1 `value_input` edge; both edges are `value_input`. No cycle ✓.

**Topological order:** {`party_rate_charge`, `model_change_fee`} (either order) → `extension_charge`.

**Per-edge load-bearing run:**

| edge skipped | what changes | scored value with the edge | without it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `extension ← party_rate` | `rate_charged` 119.76 → 0.00, so `extra_day_figure` falls back to `multi_day_daily_rate_usd` 39.00 instead of 23.95 | 87.73 | 120.24 |
| `extension ← model_change` | `change_fee_entries` 1 → 0, so `extension_fee_due` rises from 0 to `extension_fee_usd` 10.00 | 87.73 | 97.73 |

Both edges bear weight.

**Parallel edges.** The two out-edges of the root write disjoint row types, neither reads the other's output, and the root combines them through two independent bindings (`extra_day_figure`, `extension_fee_due`). Both orders give the same terminal state.

**No-wait argument.** Stated above under `### policy_self_consistency`.

**Tool layer judges no prerequisite.** `raise_rental_rate_charge_fcd244c0` and `raise_model_change_fee_b751c3b4` each run `ctx.make_id` → `ctx.find` → `ctx.create("rentals_ledger", …)` → `ctx.update("rentals_holdings", …, rental_balance_usd=…)` and return a confirmation string; neither branches on anything. `confirm_rental_extension_b56bb368` computes `added = max(0, new_due_date − due_date)` purely to widen `rental_days_booked`, then creates the ledger row and updates the holding; it does not test `extension_allowed`, `extension_max_days`, `status` or whether the prerequisites were written. No raise, no error return, no hint. **PASS.**

**Customer's own write.** The root itself is `owner="user"`, and the persona hands it over passively: *"The extension itself he wants to put through himself: he would rather press the button … so when the agent hands the confirmation across to him he runs it."* ✓

**Persona raises only the root.** He names the extension and nothing else. He never mentions the hire rate, a swap fee or anything owed; asked about any of it he says *"he has no idea and that is what the desk is for."* He names no further item of work, and he closes exactly where the last gold action lands: *"Once the agent tells him the skis are booked through to the twenty-third and what it comes to, he says good, thanks them for sorting it out, and rings off."* The world facts he volunteers — the request lodged on the Tuesday evening, two lessons taken so far this week, the room running to the 23rd — each match an authoritative row (`rentals_requests.7a0ec0de…`, two `lessons_session_deliver` rows, `lodging_holdings.a1338ee9….departure_date`) and none of them is a prerequisite problem. **PASS.**

| `advance_share_level` | parameter | advance-booked and multi-day → 15.00 | `reserved_date` vs `pickup_date` | 0 | 140.89 ✓ |

Five factors; three `parameter`, two `method`; multi-source in `passholder_share_level` (passes holding + passes ledger) and `bundle_share_level` (lessons holding + lodging holding); cross-difficulty into `passes` (11 seeded scan rows) and `lessons` / `lodging` (both seeded), each consistent with its own product charter.
**Near-miss:** `passes_ledger` rows `f0bb1932…` (2026-10-24) and `56eaf473…` (2026-10-31) sit three months and a few days before `NOW`; a careless reader counts 11 scans instead of 9. Both readings clear the threshold of 6, so the near-miss tests the window without moving the tier.
**No stamp:** no field names a day rate band, a share level or a bundle outcome.

**Closest alternative candidates, excluded on policy and world evidence.**

- *Pricing the extension straight off the package's rate card: 5 × 39.00 + 10.00 = 205.00.* Excluded by the root's two prerequisite sentences, which fix the moment of the charge as after the hire rate stands on the account and after every change of model carries its fee; once both stand, `extra_day_figure` is 119.76 / 5 = 23.95 and `extension_fee_due` is 0.
- *Charging the hire rate for the three dates the kit has been out rather than the five days of the agreement.* Excluded by `rentals_ext_party_rate_charge.rule`: "Where the account carries at least one date the kit was out and the agreement stands with the kit out, the days charged for are instead the length of the agreement" — three `rentals_day_consume` rows stand and `status = "picked_up"`.
- *Adding the lesson and lodging bundle shares together (25 %).* Excluded by "the larger of the package's lesson bundle share and its lodging bundle share is taken off, and the two are never added together", which also carries base `rentals_agg_party_pricing`'s "only the largest is taken".
- *Taking the post-stay share of 110 %.* Excluded by "whose departure date falls **on or after** the date the guest has asked the kit to be kept to": `departure_date` is 2027-02-23, exactly the date asked for.
- *Counting the two late-October scans inside the three-month window (11 rather than 9).* Both readings clear the threshold of 6, so the tier is unchanged; the rule's window words exclude them all the same.
- *Taking the size-change request as the extension request.* Excluded by `request_type`; `rentals_requests.499652cb…` carries no `requested_due_date` at all.

## findings

### T1-1 — the charter-global undeclared override F-3 does not bite this world

`_difficulty.md` → `### override_declarations`, finding **F-3**, records that `rentals_ext_party_rate_charge` drops base `rentals_agg_party_pricing`'s lesson-bundle-alone branch without naming it in `overwrite`. Judged against this task's world: the household holds both a lesson booking (`lessons_holdings.36401fd2-0cff-4dbc-9616-669f72164f11`, season 2026-27) and a lodging reservation (`lodging_holdings.a1338ee9-e210-4041-ae81-f6a9c2830509`, season 2026-27), so `bundle_share_level` takes its **first** tier and the dropped branch is never reached. Base and extended agree here: base says "only the largest is taken", extended says "the larger of the package's lesson bundle share and its lodging bundle share", and both give 15.00 on the Basic package.

The consequence is therefore **not demonstrable on this task**, and this task's unique-solution relationship is unaffected. The `design_rationale`'s base-invariant card for the hire-rate write states the scope of `rentals_agg_party_pricing` as "the passholder and bundle reductions and the rule that only the largest bundle reduction is taken, never both added together" and does not address the dropped branch; that silence is part of the charter-global finding, not a task-0 or task-1 consequence. Recorded here so that F-3 is not lost, and so that it is not counted twice.

### T1-2 — observation: the sensitivity figure 100.66 rounds against the rule's own stated convention

`computations[2].factor_sensitivity[2].baseline_result` records 100.66 for `residence_share_level`. Recomputing with that factor's baseline (`residence_share = 1.0`) and everything else unchanged: `3 × (23.95 × 0.90 + 12.00) = 3 × 33.555 = 100.665`. `rentals_ext_extension_charge.rule` says "The charge is worked out once and **rounded half up** to two decimal places", which gives **100.67**; the evaluator's `RND` is Python's `round()`, which is round-half-to-even and, on the binary representation 100.66499999999999, gives 100.66.

The factor bears weight on either figure (both differ from 87.73), so the relationship holds and this is not a red light. It is recorded because it is the one place in this difficulty where the charter-global rounding divergence (`_difficulty.md` → `### rule_compute_equivalence`, observation **O-2**) actually changes a printed number. No scored value of either task lands on a half-cent, so no gold figure is affected.

### T1-3 — observation: the notice tier is decided by a date subtraction over a timestamp the base charter would count in elapsed hours

`notice_share_level` tier 1 requires the extension request to have been "raised at least the early notice days before the date written on the agreement", `early_notice_days: 2`. The request `rentals_requests.7a0ec0de-ef05-47fe-af33-12a0dc1d259c` carries `created_at: "2027-02-16 18:24:00 MST"` against `due_date: "2027-02-18"`. `compute.notice_lead_days` is `MX(0, DAYS(request_raised_date, F('due_date')))`, and `DAYS` truncates both operands to their date parts, giving 2 — the early-notice tier, 0.90.

Measured as elapsed time the gap is a little over one day, which on the base charter's own habit of counting notice periods "in whole elapsed hours … an hour begun is not an hour elapsed" (base `rentals_cancellation`, base `rentals_late_return`) would give one day and the 100 % fall-through tier. The extended rule says "days … before the date written on the agreement", a date-to-date phrasing, so the derivation follows the dates and reaches the same tier GT records; the two conventions nonetheless sit side by side in one charter, and this row carries a time of day that makes the difference live. No second value is entailed on the extended rule's own words, so this is an observation rather than a red light.

### T1-4 — observation: the world sits exactly on the change allowance, where the policy's closing sentence admits a second reading

`rentals_ext_model_change_fee.rule` closes:
> "A rider who has used the package's allowance of changes is offered a new agreement at the day rate rather than a further change, and no fee under this rule arises for them."

On this world `rentals_holdings.693c8ae3….swap_count = 1` and the Basic package's `max_swaps_per_rental` is **1**, so at the moment the fee is priced the rider *has* used the package's allowance of changes. Read literally, the sentence gives `change_fee_amount_usd = 0.00` instead of 5.85 — and with it `extension_fee_due` would revert to 10.00 and the extension charge to 97.73, since `change_fee_entries` counts rows rather than amounts only if the fee is raised at all.

The reading is nevertheless self-defeating and is not adopted: on any package whose allowance is one — Junior and Basic — every rider whose change is being priced has by definition used the allowance, so the literal reading would make the change fee unchargeable on those packages and empty the policy of content for them. The sentence's evident subject is a rider seeking a *further* change, which is what "rather than a further change" says. The policy therefore still uniquely entails 5.85.

It is recorded because the seed places the rider exactly on the boundary the sentence names, which is the one configuration in which the wording carries weight it was not meant to carry. `design_rationale` does not address the allowance at all.

**Affected artifact and location.** `rentals.extended.yaml` → `rentals_ext_model_change_fee.rule`, final sentence, and `baseline.rule`, which repeats it; `tasks/1.json` → `initial_state.rentals_holdings.693c8ae3….swap_count`.

### T1-5 — observation: the agreement is three days into a package that takes its money at collection with no hire rate raised

`blueprint/products/rentals.yaml`, variant "Basic Ski & Board Rental", carries `payment_due_point: "at_pickup"`, and base `rentals_pricing` says "The package's payment point decides when the money is taken: at booking, at collection, or at hand-in." The kit was collected on 2027-02-14 and at `NOW = 2027-02-17` the account still carries no hire rate at all — which is exactly what makes the `extension ← party_rate` edge unmet, and the `design_rationale` relies on it ("the agreement's outstanding figure stands at 60.00, exactly the helmet add-on, which is only possible while the hire rate is still missing").

This is a shop that has not billed a hire three days after handing the kit over. It is not a contradiction — base fixes when money is *taken*, not when a charge is *raised*, and the helmet add-on was raised on the collection date — but the world it depends on is one in which the package's own payment point has already been missed.
